rationale: The "profitability per unit of profitability instability" ratio is a coherent quality-scaled profitability construct rather than a literal rediscovery, but it sits close to the published earnings-volatility/QMJ-stability literature and the raw ratio will be dominated by near-zero-denominator outliers, so it should be winsorized or rank-transformed before the FMB slope is believed.

Since the 0/1 indicator dominates the [0,1] rank, the sort effectively becomes "negative-accrual firms long, all positive-accrual firms short," making this a repackaging of the Sloan accruals anomaly rather than a genuine profitability-quality interaction.

A rank-product of high profitability and low leverage is the textbook profitability-plus-safety composite (QMJ), offers no mechanism beyond its two well-documented components, and is trivially constructed.

The 0–5 profitable-year count both dwarfs the [0,1] ROA rank (so the signal is mostly a coarse loss-history screen, a known effect) and saturates at 5 for most surviving firms, plus the window length is ambiguous if the panel is monthly with annual data carried forward.

Pairing Novy-Marx gross profitability with the durability of the gross margin itself is an economically motivated moat proxy on a distinct (revenue-side) channel from ROA-volatility variants, though its incremental content versus the Operating Profit Sharpe proposal must be checked and the five-year window will cost coverage.

The ROE–ROA wedge equals ib·(at−ceq)/(ceq·at), so it flips sign for loss-makers (rewarding highly levered unprofitable firms) and explodes for near-zero or negative book equity; absent those pathologies it reduces to roughly "ROA rank minus leverage rank," i.e., the additive twin of the Unlevered Profit Strength proposal.
